text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector roll (canary -> 25%), /chat/stream p95 token latency climbed ~12% over the 10:30-11:00 window. Per-token cost panel also shows a step up. I pulled a quick comparison and KV hit rate dropped ~6% on that route. Link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/gh8k/streaming-kpi?orgId=1

priya: Thanks. Which kernel variant was rolled? and any KV TTL changes around the same time?

alex: Kernel variant = kernel-v2-alpha (new heuristics: 'voting' selector + sample-based batching). No manual KV TTL changes but autoscaler adjusted shards (logs show a short rebuild). Timeline:
- 10:28: canary promotion started
- 10:31: kernel-v2-alpha at 25% routing
- 10:34: autoscaler rebuild triggered for kv-backend-3
- 10:36: perf-bot alert fired

sam: Possible hypothesis: selector caused slightly different batching alignment -> more partial cache misses (prefix splits). Also sample-based batching increases jitter; small batches -> higher per-token overhead.

maria: Can we add a quick panel that breaks token latency by kernel_id + batch_size distribution? Right now our token-latency-by-route is aggregated which hides kernel-specific deltas.

perf-bot: Alert: anomaly_detect(token_p95, window=15m) triggered for route="/chat/stream" on 1769501300. Severity=medium.

infra-bot: Noting autoscaler logs: "kv-backend-3 rebuild started" at 1769501360, completed at 1769501420. Rebuild coincides with drop in KV hit-rate.

priya: Posting two snippets to iterate quickly — a PromQL to plot kernel-specific token p95 and a billing SQL to reconcile cost-per-token by kernel: 

PromQL:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{route="/chat/stream"}[5m])) by (le, kernel_id))
```

Billing SQL (bigquery-style):
```
SELECT
  kernel_id,
  SUM(tokens) AS total_tokens,
  SUM(tokens * cost_per_token) AS estimated_cost
FROM
  `billing.events`
WHERE
  route = '/chat/stream' AND
  timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1769501200) AND TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1769501450)
GROUP BY kernel_id
ORDER BY estimated_cost DESC;
```

sam: Nice. Also let's surface KV hit-rate by prefix-length and by kernel selector decision (if available). If the selector picks different shards or alignment it might increase prefix fragmentation.

alex: I'll attach the kernel traces and a couple of mini-profiling dumps. Quick fetch command: `rdw trace get --id abc1234 --format json` (will upload to the dashboard in a bit).

maria: For dashboard changes: new panels to propose — 1) token p95 by kernel_id, 2) batch-size histogram by kernel_id, 3) kv-hit-rate by prefix_len, 4) cost-per-token waterfall (kernel cost + kv-miss surcharge). Can we add a rollback toggle in the route-level panel to re-route traffic back to kernel-v1?

infra-bot: There is a route-level rollback flag: `route.override.kernel=kernel-v1` but requires 2 reviewers for prod.

priya: Short-term plan: 1) create the kernel_id token-p95 panel (priya) 2) run the billing SQL for the window and post results (alex) 3) sam to run a small A/B with kernel-v1 vs kernel-v2-alpha at 10% each to measure KV-hit and batch distributions. 4) If cost delta > 6% or p95 delta > 8% we rollback canary.

sam: I can run the A/B now, will post a tiny replay trace with identical prompt set.

alex: Uploaded trace + kernel profile here: https://artifacts.redwood.io/traces/abc1234.json. Early glance: kernel-v2-alpha uses slightly different KV prefetch ordering which explains the prefix split.

maria: SGTM. I'll prep dashboard PR and add the waterfall visualization. :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks all — save decisions for next sync if A/B confirms. Will update the incident doc if we escalate.

alex: Thanks team. Short and focused thread — will follow up with numbers when the billing query returns.
